Hex-bin point counts over any study-area boundary

Source: R/hrr.R
mysterymaps_hex_bin_counts.Rd

Builds a hexagonal grid over boundary_sf, counts how many points_sf fall in each cell, and returns the cells that cleared min_count – the GEOLYTIX-style "bin points into hexagons, shade by count" map, generalized from the HRR/physician case in mysterymaps_hrr_maps() to any boundary and any point dataset. It is a thin, renaming wrapper around mm_honeycomb_counts(), which carries the tested fixes (coastline slivers under s2, the westernmost-cells defect, CRS transforms); this function adds no new hex-counting logic of its own.

Usage

mysterymaps_hex_bin_counts(
  boundary_sf,
  points_sf,
  value_col = "count",
  cellsize = 0.3,
  min_count = 1L,
  southern_limit = -90,
  include_zero_cells = FALSE
)

Arguments

boundary_sf

sf: polygon(s) defining the study area the grid is built over and clipped to.

points_sf

sf: point data to count per hex cell. Transformed to boundary_sf's CRS automatically if it arrives in another one.

value_col

character(1): name of the output count column. Default "count".

cellsize

numeric(1): hexagon size in the units of boundary_sf's CRS (degrees, if left in EPSG:4326). Default 0.3.

min_count

integer(1): cells holding fewer than this many points are dropped rather than returned – small-cell suppression, not a rendering detail. Default 1L (no suppression). Ignored when include_zero_cells = TRUE (see below).

southern_limit

numeric(1): cells entirely south of this latitude are dropped. mm_honeycomb_counts() defaults this to 15 to cut outlying US territory out of HRR maps; that is wrong for a boundary that is not the continental US (it would silently delete most of the Southern Hemisphere), so this wrapper defaults to -90, i.e. no clipping.

include_zero_cells

logical(1): return every hex cell in boundary_sf, including ones no point fell in, with value_col = 0 there, instead of silently omitting them. Default FALSE, matching mm_honeycomb_counts()'s original point-counting behaviour. A reader cannot tell "zero, measured" from "not drawn" on a map with gaps in the grid – the distinction mysterymaps_jenks_zero_scale() and mysterymaps_hex_bin_rate() both exist to preserve. min_count does not apply in this mode: suppressing small counts and asserting that a cell is a true zero are different, incompatible claims about the same cell.

Value

An sf of hex cells carrying a value_col count column. With the default include_zero_cells = FALSE, cells with fewer than min_count points are not returned at all; with include_zero_cells = TRUE, every cell in boundary_sf is returned, zero-count ones included.

See also

mysterymaps_hrr_maps(), which wraps mm_honeycomb_counts() for the HRR/physician use case with AK/HI/PR insets baked in; mysterymaps_hex_bin_rate(), which always returns the full grid because a rate needs to distinguish zero from missing.

Other geospatial: mm_area_in(), mm_honeycomb_counts(), mysterymaps_hex_bin_rate(), validate_sf_inputs()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
mysterymaps_hex_bin_counts(boundary_sf, points_sf, value_col = "flood_risk")
mysterymaps_hex_bin_counts(boundary_sf, points_sf, include_zero_cells = TRUE)
}
